title: Full Business Lifecycle Synchronization
brief: Wires all 10 broken cross-engine transitions so data flows automatically from quote to cash with zero manual re-entry. Archaeology audit found 7 of 10 direct sync points broken (quote→order, order→job, job→material PO, job→schedule, scrap→cost, job-complete→invoice, payment→GL) plus 3 feedback loops missing (actual cost→quote calibration, tool wear→life model, cycle time→schedule estimate). Adds BusinessSyncEngine as a central event bus to make all sync points reliable through refactoring, CashFlowProjectionEngine for rolling 30/60/90-day AR+AP projection, and BurdenRateEngine for machine burden rates from GL actuals.

phases.title: Direct Sync Transitions (SYNC-01 through SYNC-07)
phases.description: Wire the 7 broken direct engine-to-engine data handoffs: quote acceptance auto-creates an order, order creation auto-creates jobs with routing, job creation triggers inventory check and PO if short, job creation auto-schedules to machine via EDD, scrap recording auto-adjusts job cost, job completion auto-creates invoice and posts to GL, and payment recording auto-posts the double-entry GL debit/credit pair.

units.title: Quote Acceptance → Order Auto-Creation (SYNC-01)

steps.instruction: Read QuoteRevisionEngine.ts in full — locate changeStatus() method, understand its parameter signature and what it currently does on status transitions
Read OrderManagerEngine.ts — locate createOrder() signature, identify required fields: customer_id, line_items (array), due_date, source_quote_id, total_value

In QuoteRevisionEngine.changeStatus(), add a branch: when newStatus === 'accepted' and current status is not already 'accepted', import orderManagerEngine lazily (await import('../OrderManagerEngine.js')) and call createOrder({ customer_id: quote.customer_id, line_items: quote.line_items, due_date: quote.due_date, source_quote_id: quote.id, total_value: quote.total_price })

After createOrder() returns, validate: Math.abs(order.total_value - quote.total_price) <= 0.01 — if outside tolerance throw an Error('Order value $X diverges from quote $Y by more than $0.01') and roll back by calling cancelOrder(order.id)
Store the returned order.id on the quote as quote.order_id and call persist() so the linkage survives restart
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors
Write a unit test: call changeStatus(quoteId, 'accepted'), assert orderManagerEngine.getOrder() returns an order with total_value matching quote.total_price within $0.01

deliverables.description: changeStatus('accepted') auto-calls orderManagerEngine.createOrder() and validates price match within $0.01

exit_conditions: Accepting a quote in QuoteRevisionEngine.changeStatus() automatically creates an order via OrderManagerEngine
order.total_value === quote.total_price within $0.01 — mismatch throws and rolls back
quote.order_id is set and persisted after successful order creation
npm run build:fast produces 0 errors
abort_criteria: QuoteRevisionEngine has no changeStatus() method — locate the equivalent status-transition method and apply the hook there
OrderManagerEngine.createOrder() requires fields not present on the quote object — map what is available and add TODO for missing fields

units.title: Order → Job + Routing Auto-Creation (SYNC-02)

steps.instruction: Read OrderManagerEngine.ts — locate createOrder() and identify where the order is saved and persist() is called
Read JobLifecycleEngine.ts — locate createJob() signature: identify required fields (order_id, part_number, routing_steps, estimated_hours, due_date, qty)

After the order is saved in createOrder(), iterate order.line_items — for each item where item.type === 'manufactured' (or equivalent producible flag), lazily import jobLifecycleEngine and call createJob({ order_id: order.id, part_number: item.part_number, qty: item.qty, routing_steps: item.operations ?? [], due_date: order.due_date })

Calculate estimated_hours per job: sum each routing step's (cycle_time_min * qty / 60) + (setup_time_min / 60). Default cycle_time_min = 0 and setup_time_min = 0 if absent on a step — do not throw for missing times
Collect all created job IDs into order.job_ids array and persist the order after all jobs are created
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors

Write a unit test: create an order with 2 manufactured line items each having 3 routing steps, assert 2 jobs are created with correct estimated_hours = Σ(cycle_time × qty / 60) + (setup_time / 60) per step

deliverables.description: createOrder() auto-creates one job per manufactured line item with routing steps and calculated estimated_hours

exit_conditions: Creating an order with manufactured line items auto-creates one job per item via JobLifecycleEngine.createJob()
job.estimated_hours = Σ(step.cycle_time × qty / 60) + (step.setup_time / 60) for all routing steps
order.job_ids array is populated and persisted
npm run build:fast produces 0 errors
abort_criteria: JobLifecycleEngine.createJob() throws synchronously on missing routing_steps — wrap with try/catch and log a warning rather than failing the entire order creation

units.title: Job → Inventory Check → Auto-PO (SYNC-03)

steps.instruction: Read JobLifecycleEngine.ts — locate createJob() and identify where job is saved. Read InventoryOptimizationEngine.ts — find checkAvailability(material_id, qty_needed) or equivalent method
Read PurchaseOrderEngine.ts — find createPO() signature: identify required fields (vendor_id, line_items, material_id, qty, unit_cost, due_date)

After job is saved in createJob(), for each routing step that references a material_id (or for the job's primary material), call inventoryOptimizationEngine.checkAvailability(material_id, required_qty). Capture shortage = max(0, required_qty - available_qty)

If shortage > 0, calculate EOQ = Math.sqrt(2 * demand * order_cost / holding_cost). Use demand = shortage (immediate need), order_cost = material.default_order_cost_usd ?? 50, holding_cost = material.unit_cost * 0.25 (25% carrying rate). Order qty = Math.max(shortage, EOQ), rounded up to nearest integer
Call purchaseOrderEngine.createPO({ job_id: job.id, material_id, qty: orderQty, vendor_id: material.preferred_vendor_id ?? 'DEFAULT', due_date: job.due_date, auto_generated: true })
Store returned po_id on job.auto_po_ids array and persist the job
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors
Write a unit test: set inventory level to 0, create a job needing 50 units of material. Assert a PO is created with qty >= 50 and qty >= EOQ(50, order_cost, holding_cost)

deliverables.description: createJob() checks inventory via InventoryOptimizationEngine; auto-creates PO via PurchaseOrderEngine when shortage exists, using EOQ formula
checkAvailability() returns available qty for material (verify method exists, add if absent)
createPO() accepts auto_generated flag and job_id linkage (verify and add fields if absent)

exit_conditions: Job creation with material shortage auto-creates a PO via PurchaseOrderEngine
PO qty = max(shortage, EOQ) where EOQ = sqrt(2DS/H), D=shortage, S=order_cost, H=unit_cost×0.25
No PO created when inventory is sufficient
job.auto_po_ids is populated and persisted
npm run build:fast produces 0 errors
abort_criteria: InventoryOptimizationEngine has no checkAvailability() — search for equivalent method name, adapt accordingly
PurchaseOrderEngine.createPO() signature is incompatible — add an overload or wrapper rather than changing the existing signature

units.title: Job → Auto-Schedule to Machine (SYNC-04)

steps.instruction: Read CapacityPlanningEngine.ts — locate scheduleJob() or findBestMachineSlot() method. Identify required parameters: machine_type, estimated_hours, due_date, priority

In JobLifecycleEngine.createJob(), after the inventory check (U-BIZ48), call capacityPlanningEngine.scheduleJob({ machine_type: job.machine_type ?? job.routing_steps[0]?.machine_type, estimated_hours: job.estimated_hours, due_date: job.due_date, priority: job.priority ?? 'normal' })
The scheduler must use EDD (Earliest Due Date) ordering: among all machines of the required type, pick the one whose next available slot ends earliest while still completing before job.due_date
Apply results to job: job.scheduled_start = result.start_time, job.scheduled_end = result.end_time, job.assigned_machine = result.machine_id
If no machine has capacity before due_date, set job.schedule_status = 'capacity_risk' and log a warning — do not throw, the job still gets created
Persist the job with scheduling fields populated
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors
Write a unit test: register 2 machines of same type with different availability windows, create a job — assert it is scheduled to the machine whose slot ends earliest, and job.assigned_machine is set

deliverables.description: createJob() auto-schedules to best-fit machine via CapacityPlanningEngine using EDD; sets scheduled_start, scheduled_end, assigned_machine on job
scheduleJob() implements EDD selection among machines of the required type (verify or enhance)

exit_conditions: New jobs receive scheduled_start, scheduled_end, assigned_machine automatically on creation
Machine selected by EDD: earliest slot that fits estimated_hours before due_date
Capacity-risk jobs get schedule_status='capacity_risk' rather than throwing
npm run build:fast produces 0 errors
abort_criteria: CapacityPlanningEngine has no scheduleJob() — implement a minimal EDD slot-finder inline in JobLifecycleEngine and add a TODO to refactor into CapacityPlanningEngine

units.title: Scrap → Auto Cost Adjustment (SYNC-05)

steps.instruction: Read TimeClockEngine.ts — locate jobStop() method. Check if scrap_count is already a parameter (it should be from BIZ-MS0 U-BIZ04). Read ActualCostEngine.ts — locate recordCost() or equivalent method that accepts job_id and a cost breakdown

In TimeClockEngine.jobStop(), after the entry is saved, check if params.scrap_count > 0. If so, retrieve the job's material_cost_per_part from JobLifecycleEngine (lazily imported): material_cost_per_part = job.material_cost / job.qty
Calculate scrap_material_cost = params.scrap_count * material_cost_per_part

Calculate scrap_labor_cost: retrieve the elapsed time entry labor_cost (entry.elapsed_hours * employee.hourly_rate). scrap_labor_cost = (params.scrap_count / (params.good_parts + params.scrap_count)) * labor_cost. If total_parts = 0, scrap_labor_cost = 0

Call actualCostEngine.recordScrapCost(job_id, { scrap_count: params.scrap_count, material_cost: scrap_material_cost, labor_cost: scrap_labor_cost, recorded_by: entry.employee_id, recorded_at: new Date().toISOString() })
Validate cost conservation: total_cost_before === good_parts_cost + scrap_cost (within $0.01 rounding). Log a warning if conservation fails — do not throw
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors

Write a unit test: stop a job with good_parts=90, scrap_count=10, material_cost_per_part=$5, total_labor=$100. Assert scrap_material_cost=$50, scrap_labor_cost=$10 (10/100 × $100), and ActualCostEngine received recordScrapCost with those values

deliverables.description: jobStop() auto-calls actualCostEngine.recordScrapCost() when scrap_count > 0, with material and labor cost breakdown
recordScrapCost() method accepts scrap cost breakdown and persists it (verify or add)

exit_conditions: Calling jobStop() with scrap_count > 0 auto-records scrap cost via ActualCostEngine
scrap_material_cost = scrap_count × material_cost_per_part
scrap_labor_cost = (scrap_count / total_parts) × total_labor_cost
Cost conservation check: good_parts_cost + scrap_cost = total_cost within $0.01
npm run build:fast produces 0 errors
abort_criteria: ActualCostEngine has no recordScrapCost() — add it as a thin wrapper around the existing recordCost() with category='scrap'

units.title: Job Complete → Auto-Invoice + GL Post (SYNC-06)

steps.instruction: Read JobLifecycleEngine.ts — find _onJobComplete() or the method called when job status transitions to 'complete'. Read InvoicingEngine.ts — find fromJobCost() or createInvoice() signature. Read GeneralLedgerEngine.ts — find recordInvoice() signature and understand chart of accounts (AR=1200, Revenue=4000, COGS=5000, WIP=1400)
In _onJobComplete(), after ActualCostEngine has the final cost (ensure actualCostEngine.getJobCost(job.id) is callable and returns total_cost with breakdown), lazy-import invoicingEngine

Call invoicingEngine.fromJobCost({ job_id: job.id, customer_id: job.customer_id, actual_cost: cost.total, markup_rate: job.markup_rate ?? 0.30, line_items: cost.breakdown, due_date: addDays(new Date(), 30) })
invoice_total = actual_cost * (1 + markup_rate). Validate: invoice_total > 0 and invoice_total >= actual_cost

After invoice is created, call generalLedgerEngine.recordInvoice({ invoice_id: invoice.id, revenue: invoice_total, cogs: cost.total }). This posts: Debit AR (1200) += invoice_total, Credit Revenue (4000) += invoice_total, Debit COGS (5000) += cost.total, Credit WIP (1400) += cost.total
Validate GL balance: sum of all debit entries === sum of all credit entries within $0.01 after each recordInvoice() call. Log a warning if out of balance — do not throw
Calculate and verify: gross_margin = (invoice_total - cost.total) / invoice_total. Assert gross_margin >= 0 (invoice covers cost). Log a warning if negative margin
Persist job.invoice_id = invoice.id and call persist()
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors
Write a unit test: complete a job with actual_cost=$1000, markup=30%. Assert invoice_total=$1300, GL AR debit=$1300, Revenue credit=$1300, COGS debit=$1000, WIP credit=$1000, gross_margin=23.08%

deliverables.description: _onJobComplete() auto-creates invoice via InvoicingEngine and posts Debit AR / Credit Revenue / Debit COGS / Credit WIP to GeneralLedgerEngine
fromJobCost() accepts actual_cost + markup_rate and returns invoice with total = actual_cost × (1 + markup) (verify or add)
recordInvoice() posts double-entry: Debit AR 1200, Credit Revenue 4000, Debit COGS 5000, Credit WIP 1400 (verify or add)

exit_conditions: Job completion auto-creates an invoice with invoice_total = actual_cost × (1 + markup_rate)
GL double-entry posted: Debit AR, Credit Revenue, Debit COGS, Credit WIP
GL trial balance remains balanced within $0.01 after the post
gross_margin = (revenue - COGS) / revenue is computed and logged
job.invoice_id is persisted
npm run build:fast produces 0 errors
abort_criteria: GeneralLedgerEngine does not track account balances (only logs transactions) — implement a running balance Map keyed by account number alongside existing log
InvoicingEngine.fromJobCost() does not exist — implement it as a new method rather than changing existing createInvoice() signature

units.title: Payment → GL Auto-Post (SYNC-07)

steps.instruction: Read InvoicingEngine.ts — locate recordPayment() method. Check if it currently posts to GeneralLedgerEngine. Read GeneralLedgerEngine.ts — verify or add recordPayment(invoice_id, amount) method
In InvoicingEngine.recordPayment(invoice_id, amount), after marking the invoice as paid, lazily import generalLedgerEngine
Call generalLedgerEngine.recordPayment({ invoice_id, amount, debit_account: 1000, credit_account: 1200 }). This posts: Debit Cash (account 1000) += amount, Credit AR (account 1200) -= amount

After recordPayment(), call generalLedgerEngine.validateTrialBalance() — returns { balanced: boolean, debit_total: number, credit_total: number, delta: number }. If Math.abs(delta) > 0.01, log an error with the delta amount but do not throw (payment is already recorded)
Persist the updated invoice with payment details (paid_at, payment_amount, gl_posted: true)
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors
Write a unit test: record a payment of $1300 against an invoice. Assert GL Debit Cash +$1300, GL Credit AR -$1300, trial balance delta = $0.00 (i.e., balanced to penny)

deliverables.description: recordPayment() auto-posts Debit Cash (1000) / Credit AR (1200) to GeneralLedgerEngine and validates trial balance
recordPayment() and validateTrialBalance() methods added/verified

exit_conditions: Calling InvoicingEngine.recordPayment() auto-posts Debit Cash (1000) and Credit AR (1200) to GeneralLedgerEngine
GL trial balance validated after every payment post — delta must be $0.00 to penny
invoice.gl_posted = true is persisted
npm run build:fast produces 0 errors
abort_criteria: GeneralLedgerEngine has no validateTrialBalance() — implement it by summing all debit and credit entries in the GL log and comparing totals

scrutiny_focus: Data integrity: every sync transition is atomic — if downstream fails, upstream does not silently succeed
Math correctness: invoice = cost × (1 + markup); GL double-entry balances to penny; scrap cost conservation
No circular imports: use lazy dynamic imports (await import()) for all cross-engine calls
Error handling: downstream failures log warnings and set status flags, they do not crash the triggering operation

phases.title: Feedback Loops (SYNC-08 through SYNC-10)
phases.description: Wire the 3 missing continuous-improvement feedback loops: actual job costs calibrate future quote estimates via exponential smoothing, actual tool life data updates Weibull and Taylor parameters via MLE, and actual cycle times update routing estimates via exponential smoothing. All three use alpha=0.2 smoothing factor.

units.title: Actual → Quote Calibration Feedback Loop (SYNC-08)

steps.instruction: Read QuoteAnalyticsEngine.ts — locate or add a recordActuals() method that accepts { job_id, quote_id, actual_cost, estimated_cost, actual_hours, estimated_hours, actual_material, estimated_material }
In JobLifecycleEngine._onJobComplete(), after ActualCostEngine has final costs, check if job.quote_id is set. If yes, lazily import quoteAnalyticsEngine
Build the actuals payload: for each cost category (labor, material, overhead), compute variance_pct = (actual - estimated) / estimated * 100
Call quoteAnalyticsEngine.recordActuals({ job_id, quote_id: job.quote_id, variances: { labor: labor_variance_pct, material: material_variance_pct, overhead: overhead_variance_pct } })

In QuoteAnalyticsEngine.recordActuals(), apply exponential smoothing per category: calibration_factor[category] = 0.8 * calibration_factor[category] + 0.2 * (1 + variance_pct / 100). Default calibration_factor = 1.0 for new categories
Persist the updated calibration_factors Map so they survive restarts. Add ENTITY_CONFIGS entry in BusinessStore.ts for 'quote_calibration_factors' if not present
Expose getCalibrationFactors() method on QuoteAnalyticsEngine so QuoteEstimatorEngine can apply them: estimated_cost_adjusted = base_estimate * calibration_factor[category]
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors

Write a unit test: start with calibration_factor=1.0. Record 5 jobs where actual labor is always 20% over estimate. Assert calibration_factor converges toward 1.20 using 0.8×old + 0.2×new formula. After 5 iterations: 1.0→1.04→1.072→1.098→1.118→1.134 (approx). Verify final value > 1.10

deliverables.description: _onJobComplete() calls quoteAnalyticsEngine.recordActuals() when job has a linked quote_id
recordActuals() applies exponential smoothing α=0.2 per cost category; getCalibrationFactors() exposes current multipliers

exit_conditions: Every completed job with a quote_id auto-calls QuoteAnalyticsEngine.recordActuals()
variance_pct = (actual - estimated) / estimated * 100 computed per cost category
calibration_factor updated with formula: 0.8 × old + 0.2 × (1 + variance_pct/100)
Calibration factors persist across server restarts
npm run build:fast produces 0 errors
abort_criteria: QuoteAnalyticsEngine has no recordActuals() — add the method; it is a new capability
Job has no quote_id linkage — add quote_id as an optional field on the Job interface and set it in OrderManagerEngine when order has source_quote_id

units.title: Tool Wear → Life Model Update (SYNC-09)

steps.instruction: Read StochasticToolLifeEngine.ts — identify Weibull parameters (beta shape, eta scale) and Taylor parameters (n exponent, C constant). Locate where these are stored and whether they are updateable
Create or locate a recordToolReplacement(tool_id, actual_life_minutes, parts_cut, failure_mode, cutting_speed_m_per_min) method in StochasticToolLifeEngine (add if absent)

In TimeClockEngine.ts or a ToolUsageEngine (whichever tracks tool replacements), when a tool is recorded as replaced or consumed during a job, lazily import stochasticToolLifeEngine and call recordToolReplacement()
In StochasticToolLifeEngine.recordToolReplacement(), append the data point to a tool_life_observations[tool_id] array and call updateWeibullParameters(tool_id)

Implement updateWeibullParameters(tool_id): use MLE for Weibull. With n observations t_1..t_n, the MLE equations are: beta_hat = n / (Σ ln(t_i/eta_hat)); iterate via Newton-Raphson (max 50 iterations, convergence threshold 1e-6). Seed with beta_init=2.0, eta_init=mean(observations)

Implement updateTaylorParameters(tool_id, cutting_speed, actual_life_minutes): use the Taylor equation VT^n = C. With each new (V, T) data point, update via log-linear regression over all stored points: ln(T) = ln(C)/n - (1/n)*ln(V). Recalculate n_taylor and C from least-squares slope/intercept of ln(V) vs ln(T)
Persist updated Weibull and Taylor parameters per tool_id. Add ENTITY_CONFIGS for 'tool_life_parameters' in BusinessStore.ts
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors

Write a unit test: supply 10 synthetic Weibull(beta=2.5, eta=300) observations. Call recordToolReplacement 10 times. Assert the fitted beta_hat is within 0.3 of 2.5 and eta_hat is within 30 minutes of 300 (MLE convergence tolerance for small n)

deliverables.description: recordToolReplacement() stores observation, runs Weibull MLE and Taylor log-linear regression, persists updated parameters per tool_id
Tool replacement event triggers stochasticToolLifeEngine.recordToolReplacement() (or ToolUsageEngine if that is where replacements are tracked)

exit_conditions: Tool replacement events call stochasticToolLifeEngine.recordToolReplacement() with actual life data
Weibull MLE converges (Newton-Raphson, max 50 iterations, 1e-6 threshold); updates beta and eta per tool
Taylor log-linear regression recalculates n and C from all observations
Parameters persisted across restarts
npm run build:fast produces 0 errors
abort_criteria: StochasticToolLifeEngine uses pre-loaded Weibull tables with no runtime update path — add a tool_life_override Map that takes precedence over table lookups for tools with >= 3 observations
Newton-Raphson diverges for small n (<3 observations) — fall back to method of moments: beta_mom = 1.2 / CV where CV = std/mean, eta_mom = mean / Γ(1 + 1/beta_mom)

units.title: Cycle Time → Schedule Estimate Update (SYNC-10)

steps.instruction: Read JobLifecycleEngine.ts — in _onJobComplete(), identify how routing_steps are stored on the job and whether actual_time_per_step is tracked. Check if TimeClockEngine job entries have per-step time breakdowns or only total time

For each routing step on the completed job, retrieve actual_time_min from the job's time tracking records. If only total time is available, distribute proportionally by estimated_time: actual_step_time = total_actual_time * (step.estimated_time / sum_estimated_times)

Apply exponential smoothing to update the routing step estimate: step.estimated_time_min = 0.8 * step.estimated_time_min + 0.2 * actual_step_time_min. Use alpha=0.2 as specified. Do not update if actual_step_time_min <= 0 or is clearly an outlier (> 5x current estimate)
Write back the updated routing step times to a routing_estimates store. Add a getRoutingEstimate(part_number, step_index) method that future job creation calls can use to pre-populate estimated_hours
Persist the routing_estimates Map. Add ENTITY_CONFIGS in BusinessStore.ts for 'routing_estimates'
Wire job creation (U-BIZ47) to call getRoutingEstimate() instead of using raw step.cycle_time when an estimate exists — if no stored estimate, fall back to step.cycle_time
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors

Write a unit test: seed a routing estimate at 60 min. Record 5 jobs with actual time 50 min each. Assert estimate converges: 60→58→56.4→55.1→54.1→53.3 (approx). Verify final estimate < 54 min after 5 iterations

deliverables.description: _onJobComplete() updates routing_estimates via exponential smoothing α=0.2 per step; createJob() reads updated estimates from routing_estimates store

exit_conditions: Every completed job updates routing step estimates via: Ê(t+1) = 0.8 × Ê(t) + 0.2 × actual
Outlier guard: actual > 5x estimate is skipped with a warning log
getRoutingEstimate() returns smoothed estimate when available; falls back to step.cycle_time when not
Routing estimates persist across restarts
npm run build:fast produces 0 errors
abort_criteria: Routing steps have no step_index or unique key — use step.operation_code or step.machine_type + step.sequence as composite key for the estimates Map

scrutiny_focus: Math correctness: exponential smoothing alpha=0.2 formula verified with numeric trace
Weibull MLE Newton-Raphson convergence tested with synthetic observations
Taylor log-linear regression: ln(V) vs ln(T) least-squares verified
Outlier handling: 5x guard on cycle time, minimum observation count on Weibull MLE

phases.title: Infrastructure — Event Bus + Projection Engines
phases.description: Create BusinessSyncEngine as a central publish/subscribe event bus that all 10 sync points can fire through, ensuring they survive refactoring of direct imports. Create CashFlowProjectionEngine for rolling 30/60/90-day AR+AP cash projection. Create BurdenRateEngine for machine burden rates calculated from GL actuals.

units.title: Create BusinessSyncEngine — Central Event Bus

steps.instruction: Check ENGINE_DIGEST.md for any existing event bus or pub/sub engine before creating a new one. If none, proceed

Create src/engines/BusinessSyncEngine.ts. Define the BusinessEvent union type covering all 9 event shapes: QuoteAcceptedEvent, OrderCreatedEvent, JobCreatedEvent, JobCompletedEvent, PaymentReceivedEvent, ScrapRecordedEvent, ToolReplacedEvent, PmDueEvent, StockLowEvent. Each event has: type (string literal), payload (typed object), timestamp (ISO string), source_engine (string)

Implement BusinessSyncEngine class with: private handlers: Map<string, Array<(event: BusinessEvent) => Promise<void>>>. Method subscribe(eventType: string, handler): unsubscribe function. Method publish(event: BusinessEvent): Promise<void> — calls all registered handlers for event.type in parallel via Promise.all(), catches individual handler errors and logs them without throwing
Add publishSync(event) method that calls handlers sequentially (await each) for events that require ordered processing (e.g., invoice before GL post)
Add an event log: last 1000 events stored in a circular buffer for auditability. Method getEventLog(eventType?: string, limit?: number): BusinessEvent[]
Export singleton: export const businessSyncEngine = new BusinessSyncEngine()

Wire existing sync points from P1/P2 to also publish via businessSyncEngine: in QuoteRevisionEngine, after createOrder() succeeds, call businessSyncEngine.publish({ type: 'quote_accepted', payload: { quote_id, order_id }, ... }). Repeat for order_created, job_created, job_completed, payment_received, scrap_recorded
In StochasticToolLifeEngine (U-BIZ54), subscribe to 'tool_replaced' events to trigger recordToolReplacement() — this decouples the tool life update from direct imports
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors
Write a unit test: publish a 'quote_accepted' event, assert the registered handler is called with correct payload. Publish 3 events of different types, assert getEventLog() returns all 3 in order

deliverables.description: NEW — publish/subscribe event bus for 9 business lifecycle events; circular event log (1000 entries); parallel and sequential publish modes; singleton export

exit_conditions: BusinessSyncEngine.ts exists with subscribe(), publish(), publishSync(), getEventLog() methods
All 9 event types defined: quote_accepted, order_created, job_created, job_completed, payment_received, scrap_recorded, tool_replaced, pm_due, stock_low
Handler errors are caught and logged without throwing from publish()
All 10 sync points (from P1 and P2) also publish events through the bus
npm run build:fast produces 0 errors
abort_criteria: ENGINE_DIGEST.md shows an existing event bus engine — use it instead of creating a new one; add missing event types and the 9 business event shapes to it

rollback.procedure: git rm src/engines/BusinessSyncEngine.ts && git checkout -- src/engines/QuoteRevisionEngine.ts src/engines/OrderManagerEngine.ts src/engines/JobLifecycleEngine.ts src/engines/InvoicingEngine.ts src/engines/TimeClockEngine.ts src/engines/StochasticToolLifeEngine.ts

units.title: Create CashFlowProjectionEngine + BurdenRateEngine

steps.instruction: Check ENGINE_DIGEST.md for any existing cash flow or burden rate engine before creating new ones

Create src/engines/CashFlowProjectionEngine.ts. Core data sources: AR (from InvoicingEngine.getOpenInvoices()), AP (from PurchaseOrderEngine.getOpenPOs()), scheduled payroll (from PayrollEngine.getNextPayrollDate() and total amount), scheduled POs. Method: project(horizon_days: 30 | 60 | 90): CashFlowProjection

CashFlowProjection type: { as_of: string; opening_balance: number; daily_buckets: DailyBucket[]; summary_30: PeriodSummary; summary_60: PeriodSummary; summary_90: PeriodSummary }. DailyBucket: { date: string; inflows: CashFlowLine[]; outflows: CashFlowLine[]; net: number; running_balance: number }. CashFlowLine: { source: string; amount: number; category: 'ar' | 'ap' | 'payroll' | 'po' | 'other' }

Implement the projection formula: for each day d from 0 to horizon_days, Net(d) = Σ(inflows scheduled on day d) - Σ(outflows scheduled on day d). running_balance(d) = opening_balance + Σ(Net(0..d)). AR inflows use invoice.due_date as the expected collection date. AP outflows use po.due_date. Payroll outflows use next_payroll_date + every 14 days thereafter
PeriodSummary: { total_inflows, total_outflows, net_cash_flow, ending_balance, lowest_balance_date, lowest_balance_amount }. Flag periods where lowest_balance_amount < 0 with risk_flag: true
Export singleton: export const cashFlowProjectionEngine = new CashFlowProjectionEngine(). Register with PersistenceBridge for last_projection cache

Method calculateBurdenRate(machine_id: string, period_months: number = 3): BurdenRateResult.
